## Introduction

The objective of this assignment is to practice creating structured data files by hand and loading them into R for downstream analysis. We are using data focused on diabetes management, including titles, authors, publication years, publishers, and genres. At least one book in our dataset contains multiple authors to satisfy the assignment requirements.

## Packages and Data Loading

For this assignment, we use packages designed for web scraping and data parsing to load our manually created files from GitHub.

```{r}
#| label: packages

# Loading packages
pacman::p_load(rvest, jsonlite, tidyverse, knitr, kableExtra)
```

## Loading HTML Data

We start by loading the data from our manually created HTML file. We use the raw version of the GitHub URL so that the rvest package can read the table directly into R.

```{r}
#| label: load-html

# Use the raw version of the GitHub URL
html_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dave-Melchor/Data-607-Data-Acquisition-and-Management/refs/heads/main/data/raw/books.html"

# Import HTML table directly into a data frame
html_data <- html_url |> 
  read_html() |> 
  html_table()

html_data <- html_data[[1]]

# Inspect the dataset
str(html_data)
```

```{r}
#| label: view-html-table

# Make summary table for HTML data
html_data |> 
  kbl(
    caption = "Table 1. Books Data Loaded from HTML",
    align = c("l", "l", "c", "l", "l")
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Loading JSON Data

Next, we load the same dataset from our manually created JSON file using the jsonlite package.

```{r}
#| label: load-json

# Use the raw version of the GitHub URL
json_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dave-Melchor/Data-607-Data-Acquisition-and-Management/refs/heads/main/data/raw/books.json"

# Import JSON data directly into a data frame
json_data <- fromJSON(json_url)

# Inspect the dataset
str(json_data)
```

```{r}
#| label: view-json-table

# Make summary table for JSON data
json_data |> 
  kbl(
    caption = "Table 2. Books Data Loaded from JSON",
    align = c("l", "l", "c", "l", "l")
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  ) |> 
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Comparing Data Frames

The final step requires us to compare the two data frames to determine whether they are identical.

```{r}
#| label: compare-data

# Check if both data frames are identical
identical(html_data, json_data)
```

## Conclusion

By manually creating both the HTML table and the JSON file, we can see how different file formats structure the same underlying information. While the data looks identical at a glance, checking them with `identical()` returns `FALSE`. This happens because `html_table()` reads all columns in as character strings by default, whereas .`json` preserves numeric data types like integers.
